newsitem.title: USA: Marion Cty, Fla., to vote on sales tax for schools.
newsitem.headline: Marion Cty, Fla., to vote on sales tax for schools.

text.p: Florida's Marion County has scheduled a June 10 referendum on a half-cent sales tax increase to raise money for school construction, Ocala Star-Banner reported Wednesday.

The tax would remain in effect 20 years, raising an estimated $58 million in the first five years. It is part of a five-year, $180 million capital improvement plan that would build four new schools and expand 16 others.
The school board is still considering whether to issue revenue bonds backed by the sales tax or to use certificates of participation to finance construction.
The district has 44 schools and about $110 million in debt outstanding, including $25 million of COPs.
The county school board unanimously approved the sales taxreferendum, which was proposed by a community task force studying ways to meet student demand in the rapidly growing area.
By law, if votes approve the sales tax increase, property tax rates would be frozen for three years.

Eleven Florida school districts have proposed similar sales tax hikes for schools in the last three years. Manatee, Okaloosa, Monroe and Jackson counties passed them on the first attempt, while Hillsborough and St. Lucie counties approved them on the second try.
Voters in Broward, Pasco, Leon, DeSoto and Alachua counties rejected sales tax hikes.
